content.title: About
content.content: Yokan is a traditional Japanese jelly‑like dessert made from agar‑agar, sugar and sweet red bean paste (anko). It has a firm, slightly springy texture and a mild sweetness, usually served in small cubes.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Yokan originated in Japan during the Edo period and was originally a treat for the aristocracy.
Traditional yokan uses red bean paste, but there are variations with green tea, pumpkin, and black sesame.
The agar‑agar used in yokan is derived from seaweed, making the dessert vegan.
Yokan is often packaged in lacquered boxes as a gift.
In Japan yokan is commonly enjoyed with green tea, as its sweetness balances the tea’s bitterness.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Yokan contains virtually no fat, making it a light dessert option.

items.title: Source of plant protein
items.content: Red bean paste provides a modest amount of plant‑based protein.

items.title: Rich in fiber
items.content: Red beans are a good source of dietary fiber, supporting digestion.

items.title: Contains antioxidants
items.content: Phytonutrients in the beans help combat oxidative stress.

items.title: Gluten‑ and lactose‑free
items.content: Yokan is suitable for people with gluten or lactose intolerance.

items.title: Legume allergy
items.content: Some individuals may be allergic to red beans.

items.title: High sugar content
items.content: Traditional yokan is sweetened, so it should be consumed in moderation.

items.title: Agar‑agar sensitivity
items.content: Large amounts of agar‑agar can cause mild digestive upset in sensitive people.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Yokan is typically cut into small cubes and served as a light dessert after a meal. It can be eaten on its own, paired with tea, or used as a filling for sweet rolls.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store yokan in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2 weeks. For longer storage, freeze it in a tightly sealed bag and thaw at room temperature before serving.
